title: Titanium Ultrasonic Nodal Clamp Ring
alloyReason: Triaxially forged Titanium Ultrasonic Nodal Clamp Ring (UNS R56400) is specified for this ultrasonic tooling component where isotropic mechanical properties are mandatory for withstanding multi-axial stress states. The 3D forging process eliminates crystallographic texture directionality, delivering uniform 950 MPa tensile strength and >15% elongation in all three orientations. This is critical for Stack clamping nodal ring flange (Grade 4) where fatigue crack initiation is sensitive to microstructural anisotropy. This rationale is driven by stack clamping nodal ring flange (grade 4) and service environment demands.
process: CNC turn-mill multi-axis for ultrasonic tooling geometry
Shot peening Almen for net-shape tolerance
Black oxide/DLC coating for net-shape tolerance
CMM SPC dimensional check for net-shape tolerance
surfaceTreatment: DLC coating 2um, 15GPa hardness, 0.1mu friction coefficient applied to wear surfaces for extended durability — tailored for stack clamping nodal application
commonFailures: Brinelling of Al housing from steel insert - resolved by steel-backed bronze bushing SAE 841 0.05mm interfer — critical for stack clamping nodal performance

faq.q: What weight-to-strength ratio does Titanium Ultrasonic Nodal Clamp Ring offer over steel?
faq.a: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V provides 40-45% weight reduction versus 4130/4340 steel at equivalent strength: 4.43 g/cm³ vs 7.85 g/cm³ with 830 MPa yield. For stack clamping nodal, this translates directly to reduced unsprung mass (suspension) or reduced reciprocating mass (valvetrain), improving both acceleration response and fatigue-limited component life by 2-3×.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Ultrasonic Nodal Clamp Ring?
faq.a: Each Titanium Ultrasonic Nodal Clamp Ring shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for stack clamping nodal.
